editorial:
Imagine a messy love triangle where the two men fighting for the same woman are both doctors. You get to follow Juliette, a free spirit who works as a hairdresser and can't seem to make up her mind. First, she is with the older doctor, Raoul, but then she catches feelings for the younger one, Clément. It is a real emotional rollercoaster because these men aren't just fighting with words; they are using their status and guilt to pull her back and forth. The vibe is very romantic but also quite sad, as you watch Juliette struggle with her own confidence while two powerful men try to claim her.

What really works here is how the movie shows the cycle of passion and regret. The acting feels natural, and the way the story jumps from the city to the countryside keeps things interesting. One downside is that the pacing slows down a bit in the middle, but the emotional payoff is worth it. If you love old-school European dramas, you should definitely check this out. It is a great pick for a rainy Sunday afternoon.
endingExplained: As the story wraps up, Juliette gets very sick with Hodgkin's disease. Even though she is surrounded by doctors, the medicine does not work. Raoul believes her sickness is actually caused by her broken heart and her chaotic love life. In the end, the tragedy hits hard because love cannot cure a physical illness. Juliette passes away, leaving the two men to deal with their grief and the memory of the woman they both loved.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves tragic romance and old French cinema.
